# NYC Land Cover 2017 (6-inch, 8 classes)

[Open in data browser](https://browser.portolan-sdi.org/#/external/data.source.coop/betanyc/nyc-land-cover-2017/land-cover-2017/collection.json) · [Source repository](https://github.com/BetaNYC/nyc-land-cover-2017) · [Report a problem](https://github.com/BetaNYC/nyc-land-cover-2017/issues) · [Hosting repository](https://source.coop/betanyc/nyc-land-cover-2017)

A 6-inch resolution, 8-class land cover map of New York City, derived from the 2017 LiDAR capture and 2016 orthoimagery. Each pixel holds one class: tree canopy, grass/shrubs, bare soil, water, buildings, roads, other impervious, or railroads. The map was made for the city's Urban Tree Canopy assessment, so it maps from the top down: canopy that hangs over a road or a building counts as tree canopy. This is a mirror of the [NYC Open Data release](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/he6d-2qns), converted without changes to pixel values to a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF in New York State Plane Long Island feet (EPSG:2263). The [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) shows how to read pixels and compute class areas without downloading the file.

## Quickstart

Read the class at a point straight from the published file (GDAL 3.x, longitude then latitude). This point in Central Park prints `2`, Grass/Shrubs:

<!-- check -->
```bash
gdallocationinfo -valonly -wgs84 \
  /vsicurl/https://data.source.coop/betanyc/nyc-land-cover-2017/land-cover-2017/nyc-land-cover-2017.tif \
  -73.9654 40.7829
```

The [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) has Python recipes for class areas in a bounding box and fast whole-city estimates.

## Classes

Pixel counts and shares are measured from the published file. Each pixel is 0.5 ft x 0.5 ft (0.25 sq ft). Shares are of pixels inside the city boundary, which includes water.

| Value | Class | Colour | Pixels | Share | Notes |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | NoData | transparent | | | Outside the New York City boundary. Transparent. |
| 1 | Tree Canopy | `#2E7D32` | 7,446,483,259 | 16.02% | Vegetation taller than 8 ft, including canopy that overhangs other features. Current as of 2017. |
| 2 | Grass/Shrubs | `#A6D96A` | 5,493,958,626 | 11.82% | Vegetation 8 ft or lower. |
| 3 | Bare Soil | `#C8A165` | 565,995,276 | 1.22% | The least accurate class: user's accuracy 89%, producer's accuracy 82%. |
| 4 | Water | `#4A90C8` | 13,237,953,060 | 28.49% |  |
| 5 | Buildings | `#B5473A` | 6,709,981,535 | 14.44% | Current as of 2017. |
| 6 | Roads | `#3F3F3F` | 4,627,975,203 | 9.96% |  |
| 7 | Other Impervious | `#A9A9A9` | 8,138,988,426 | 17.51% |  |
| 8 | Railroads | `#7E4FA0` | 249,879,655 | 0.54% | New in the 2017 map. The 2010 map folded railroads into Roads (6). Reassign 8 to 6 to compare the two years. |

## Grid and coordinate reference system

- 310,844 columns x 314,414 rows, 0.5 ft pixels, one band (`uint8`), NoData = 0.
- EPSG:2263, NAD83 / New York Long Island (ftUS). Coordinates and pixel sizes are in US survey feet, not metres.
- Overview factors: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 511, 1023, 2045 (nearest neighbour, so overview pixels are real class values).
- Extent in WGS84: -74.260381, 40.485804, -73.698025, 40.917692.

## Method and accuracy

Object-based image analysis (OBIA) with a rule-based expert system, run on the 2017 LiDAR point cloud (1-ft post spacing) and its derivatives, leaf-off 2016 4-band orthophotography (0.5-ft), and city GIS layers such as building footprints, hydrography, roadbed, railroads, parking lots, sidewalks, parks, and athletic facilities. The result was then manually reviewed and corrected. Tree canopy and buildings are current as of 2017; the other classes as of 2016.

A per-pixel accuracy assessment based on 8,493 random points indicated an overall accuracy of 98%. User's and producer's accuracies for all classes except Bare Soil exceeded 94%; for bare soil, the user's and producer's accuracies were 89 and 82%, respectively. (Source: the ArcGIS metadata in the original zip.)

## Uses

- Urban Tree Canopy assessment. The map was made for the city's updated Urban Tree Canopy assessment.
- Hazard mitigation and green infrastructure planning. The data dictionary says the dataset "will be used by several City agencies for various types of analyses, such as hazard mitigation (coastal storms, sea level rise inundation, etc.) and green infrastructure planning". It also says the dataset was collected as part of the federal Community Development Block Grant – Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) award the City received after Superstorm Sandy.
- Land cover shares by geography. The data dictionary says the dataset "may be used to assess percentage of land cover type per given geography", for example canopy or impervious share per borough, tract, or park.

## Not suited for

- Measuring all paved or built area. Mapping is top-down, so pavement and roofs under tree canopy are classed as Tree Canopy.
- Describing conditions after 2017. The map is a 2016–2017 snapshot, and this release has not changed since its publication in December 2018.
- Counting trees, or measuring tree height or species. Pixels carry a class only; Tree Canopy means vegetation over 8 ft.
- Comparing with the 2010 map class by class without first merging Railroads (8) into Roads (6).
- Fine-scale Bare Soil mapping. The source reports a producer's accuracy of 82% for Bare Soil, so about 18% of the reference Bare Soil sample points were mapped as another class.

## Known biases and uncertainty

- Tree Canopy is favoured over what lies beneath it, by design (top-down mapping). Shares of Roads, Buildings, and Other Impervious are smaller than their ground footprint where trees overhang them.
- The classes come from two dates: Tree Canopy and Buildings reflect the May 2017 LiDAR, the other classes the 2016 orthophotography.
- Bare Soil is under-mapped relative to the other classes (producer's accuracy 82%, user's accuracy 89%).
- The source publishes overall, user's, and producer's accuracies, but no confusion matrix and no per-pixel uncertainty layer.

## Known issues

- The nyc-geo-metadata page says "only vegetation < 8 ft were classed as Tree Canopy". The NYC Open Data description and the data dictionary say "> 8 ft". This catalog follows the portal and the dictionary.
- Classes are not all from the same year. Tree Canopy and Buildings are current as of 2017 (LiDAR, May 2017); the other classes as of 2016 (orthophotography).
- The source documentation defines Tree Canopy and Grass/Shrubs by height but gives no definition for Bare Soil, Water, Roads, Other Impervious, or Railroads beyond their names.
- The histogram in the source's NYC_2017_LiDAR_LandCover.img.aux.xml is scaled down. Every class count is the attribute table count divided by 21.64, and the counts sum to 2,147,483,646, just under the 32-bit integer limit. Its proportions are right, but it does not give pixel counts. Use the attribute table counts or the counts in this collection.

## License

`other`. NYC Open Data states no license for this dataset. NYC Administrative Code section 23-502(d) makes public data sets available "without any registration requirement, license requirement or restrictions on their use", and lets the city require anyone who redistributes a data set to identify its source and version and describe any changes. This catalog does both in its attribution and provenance.

- [NYC Administrative Code, Title 23, Chapter 5 (section 23-502)](https://nyc-laws.readthedocs.io/en/latest/nycadmincode/t23/c05/)
- [NYC.gov Terms of Use](https://www.nyc.gov/main/terms-of-use)

## Provenance

Mirror of [NYC Open Data he6d-2qns](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/he6d-2qns), file version 2018-12-07. Last synced 2026-10-30.

Downloaded Land_Cover.zip (1,334,211,225 bytes) from NYC Open Data he6d-2qns on 2026-10-30. The zip holds an ERDAS Imagine raster, NYC_2017_LiDAR_LandCover.img with its .ige spill file, 310,844 x 314,414 pixels of 0.5 ft. Converted with GDAL 3.13 (tools/build_cog.sh) to a COG: DEFLATE level 9 with no predictor (smaller than predictor 2 on a test window), 512 x 512 tiles, nearest-neighbour overviews, an embedded colour table, and exact statistics computed at creation. The source CRS is an unnamed Lambert Conformal Conic definition identical to EPSG:2263; the COG is labelled EPSG:2263. Pixel values are unchanged: the per-class pixel counts of the COG match the source attribute table exactly (see AGENTS.md).

Producers:

- [NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI)](https://www.nyc.gov/content/oti/pages/) (producer, licensor)
- [University of Vermont Spatial Analysis Laboratory](https://www.uvm.edu/rsenr/sal) (producer, processor)
